cases.title: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park
cases.summary: The park identifies two unauthorized ticket domains by name and warns visitors about advertisements using its identity.

events.title: Park names two ticket sellers
events.detail: Capilano says it refuses admission on tickets bought from either listed domain. Its notice directs buyers to the park and authorized partners.

cases.gap: The park’s notice gives no first-report date, registrar response or date either domain was suspended. A warning alone gives no time-to-removal measurement.

cases.title: Rotor Investments brand hijacking
cases.summary: The Manitoba Securities Commission identified a suspended website that had used the name of a real Canadian company.

events.title: Regulator confirms a suspension
events.detail: The commission says the domain used Rotor Investments Limited’s name to advertise financial services and had already been suspended when it issued the alert. The named company was the impersonated party.

cases.gap: The alert establishes suspension by November 16. It does not identify the first report, the suspension date or who requested it.

cases.title: Green P parking payment redirects
cases.summary: Stickers on public parking machines redirected people attempting to pay. The Toronto Parking Authority describes who receives the reports.

events.title: Parking authority describes the referral
events.detail: Maintenance staff and police enforcement officers flag fraudulent stickers to the parking authority. It reports them to City of Toronto Cyber Security and says the associated sites are shut down.

cases.gap: The notice describes the reporting chain but supplies no incident count or referral-to-closure dates. A municipal records lead is the parking authority’s incident/referral log for the period covered by its May warning.

cases.title: Royal Ontario Museum ticket warnings
cases.summary: The museum warns visitors about unofficial websites offering false or unauthorized ticket discounts.

events.title: Museum flags unofficial ticket discounts
events.detail: ROM’s visitor guidance directs buyers to its own tickets page and warns about third-party offers. The cited guidance identifies no individual suspect domain.

cases.gap: There is no domain-level disposition or first complaint date in this notice. Counts of counterfeit-ticket inquiries would describe a different outcome from confirmed site removals.

cases.title: Canada Revenue Agency impersonation
cases.summary: CRA describes a recurring program to remove phishing websites that impersonate the agency.

events.title: CRA describes removal volume
events.detail: The agency reports working with partners to take down hundreds of impersonating websites during the preceding year.

events.title: Annual takedown activity reported again
events.detail: CRA again describes removing hundreds of sites each year. Neither statement supplies monthly figures or the method for counting sites.

cases.gap: An existing monthly table underlying the December 2025 figure, including its definition of a website and reporting period, would supply a measurable baseline. The two announcements have overlapping coverage.

cases.title: Investment website disruption program
cases.summary: Canadian securities regulators publish cumulative counts of investment platforms and crypto scam sites they helped deactivate.

events.title: First eight months reported
events.detail: CSA reported more than 7,586 platforms and sites deactivated between June 5, 2025 and February 12, 2026.

events.title: First-year total reaches 11,728 websites
events.detail: CSA credits its joint work with CIRO for 11,728 platforms and sites deactivated from June 5, 2025 through June 5, 2026. That total includes the earlier reporting period.

cases.gap: The annual page gives 11,728 sites. Its prose refers to more than 19,860 associated URLs and its graphic gives 19,680 URLs deactivated. A reconciliation of those units and the counts of referrals by outcome would clarify the series.

cases.title: CanadianHQ marketplace shutdown
cases.summary: The CRTC traced a marketplace supplying phishing and spam services. Its public notices and a completed access request document separate steps.

events.title: CRTC opens its investigation
events.detail: The commission’s subsequent notice dates the start of its CanadianHQ investigation to January 2019.

events.title: CRTC confirms the marketplace went offline
events.detail: The commission reported that the site went offline following warrants executed in 2020 and 2021. The announcement also described penalties totalling $300,000.

events.title: 53-page release indexed
events.detail: The completed-request index lists a partial disclosure on the CanadianHQ enforcement action under number A-2021-00059. This entry describes the index record.

cases.gap: The announcement confirms a shutdown but gives no exact shutdown day. The 53-page release is an existing source to inspect before considering another request.
